verdict.tagline: A sprawling sandbox plagued by stubborn launchers and crowded lobbies.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe GTA Online as excessively grindy and expensive to acquire items.

citations.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

GTA Online is the perfect example of a game where you can spend 1000 hours and still have no idea what you're doing.

From running businesses and doing heists to buying expensive cars just to drive around the map for 10 minutes, there's always something to do. The freedom this game offers is insane.

The only downside? Rockstar's pricing, hackers, and the fact that every update makes you want to grind for another 10 hours just to afford one car.

But honestly, despite all the bugs, modders, and questionable life choices, there's nothing quite like GTA Online.

10/10 would go broke buying virtual cars again.

GTA Online is the most miserable online gaming experience I've ever had. It's extremely buggy, has incredibly unfair gameplay, is full of predatory ways to get money out of your wallet, festering with hackers and is just a boring, grindy snoozefest. I'm dumbfounded as to how this game has lasted 13+ years with the way the devs treat the game as a whole and the updates they push out. In saying that, I have 460+ hours on epic games and 200 hours on PlayStation. I love this game for reasons beyond me. It's like the toxic ex I keep coming back to, even though I know it's a bad idea. Ultimatly the decision to restrict aussies from using the free spin wheel in the Diamond Casino for no REASONABLE reason is what killed my last bit of interest in this game. Hopefully GTA 6 Online doesn't follow in it's predecessors footsteps.

GTA 5's singleplayer is PEAK and worth playing. I wish I could play it for the first time again.
Very good game although gta 6 modders glitches and grindyness kinda ruin it still a very fun game
